title: Normality of complete saturated monoid local models
statement: Let $P$ be a finitely generated integral saturated commutative monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], written additively, and suppose it is sharp, meaning that $0$ is its only invertible element. Let $n\geq0$ be an integer. For a coefficient ring $L$, write $L[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ for the ring of finite sums of symbols $c z^q t^e$, with $q\in P$, $e\in\mathbf N^n$, $c\in L$, and multiplication $z^qz^{q'}=z^{q+q'}$. If $L$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_L$, let $B_L(P,n)$ be its completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] at $(\mathfrak m_L,z^q\ (q\neq0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)$. Let $R$ be one of the following rings: (i) $B_k(P,n)$ for a field $k$; (ii) $B_C(P,n)/(\theta)$ for a Cohen ring $C$ of residue characteristic $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] and $\theta-p\in(z^q\ (q\neq0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)B_C(P,n)$. In case (ii), $p$ is prime and the residue field of $C$ is arbitrary of characteristic $p$. Then $R$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], that is, a nonzero integral domain integrally closed in its fraction field.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, the saturated complete local models; their normality is the fs local-algebra case of Kato (1994), Theorem 4.1. Kato is not in literature/: WANTED, as recorded in report.md. No non-saturated theorem from VIII 3.5 is asserted.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-sharp-fs-orthant-embedding] to $P$, obtaining $\lambda:G\hookrightarrow\mathbf Z^r$. Inside $\mathbf Z^{r+n}$ put $M=\lambda(G)\times\mathbf Z^n$ and $Q=M\cap\mathbf N^{r+n}=\lambda(P)\times\mathbf N^n$. This monoid is finitely generated: take the images of generators of $P$ and the $n$ coordinate vectors. The coefficient-preserving renaming $z^qt^e\mapsto z^{(\lambda(q),e)}$ is an isomorphism $L[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]\cong L[Q]$, with inverse supplied by the inverse of $\lambda|_P$. It carries the specified completion ideal onto $J=\mathfrak m_L L[Q]+(z^v:v\neq0)$: every nonzero pair has either $q\neq0$ or a positive $t$ exponent. Applying this isomorphism and its inverse to every quotient identifies $B_L(P,n)$ with the $J$-adic completion $T$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; Q48 agent proof of normality of these models

proof.text: Both allowable coefficient rings are complete local rings with finitely generated maximal ideal ($0$ or $(p)$): for a field the maximal ideal is $0$ and the completion is constant, and for a Cohen ring completeness is part of [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring]. Apply [lem-trf-completed-monoid-support-projection] to $M,Q$ above. It identifies $T=B_L(P,n)$ with the supported subring of $A=L[[X_1,\ldots,X_r,t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$ by $z^q\mapsto X^{\lambda(q)}$, and gives a $T$-linear retraction $\rho:A\to T$. In particular $\rho(1)=1$ and $\rho(ta)=t\rho(a)$ for $t\in T$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; Q48 agent proof of normality of these models

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete], $A$ is regular local. In case (i) put $S=A$. In case (ii) put $\Theta=\iota(\theta)$ and $\mathfrak n=(p,X_1,\ldots,X_r,t_1,\ldots,t_n)\subset A$. Every nonzero monoid element has a nonzero exponent vector, so the hypothesis on $\theta-p$ implies that $\Theta$ has constant coefficient exactly $p$. Consequently $\Theta\in\mathfrak n$ and $\Theta\notin\mathfrak n^2$: the constant coefficient of any element of $\mathfrak n^2$ belongs to $p^2C$, whereas $p\notin p^2C$, since $C$ is a domain and $p$ is a nonunit uniformizer [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring]. Now [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-hypersurface-criterion] makes $S=A/(\Theta)$ regular local. This works also for $r+n=0$, when $\Theta=p$ and $S=C/pC$.

source.place: Tags 032C (remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary), 0327 (definition-cohen-ring), and 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM); explicit constant-coefficient check by Q48

proof.text: In case (i) we already have the inclusion $R=T\hookrightarrow S=A$ and its $R$-linear retraction. In case (ii), $\rho(\Theta a)=\theta\rho(a)$ implies $T\cap\Theta A=\theta T$: if $t=\Theta a\in T$, apply $\rho$ to obtain $t=\theta\rho(a)$; the reverse inclusion is immediate. Thus $R=T/(\theta)$ embeds in $S=A/(\Theta)$, and $[a]\mapsto[\rho(a)]$ is a well-defined $R$-linear retraction $\bar\rho:S\to R$ fixing $1$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; Q48 agent proof of normality of these models

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization] to regard the regular local ring $S$ as a regular ring, then apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-normal]. Its conclusion says every prime localization of $S$ is a normal domain. At the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_S$ the canonical map $S\to S_{\mathfrak m_S}$ is an isomorphism: every denominator lies outside the unique maximal ideal and is already a unit. Therefore $S$ itself is a nonzero normal domain.

The unital injection $R\hookrightarrow S$ makes $R$ a nonzero domain and embeds $\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ into $\operatorname{Frac}(S)$. Let $x=a/b\in\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, $b\neq0$, be integral over $R$. Its same monic equation makes it integral over $S$, so $x\in S$ by the normality just proved. Apply the $R$-linear retraction of step 4 to $bx=a$: it gives $b\bar\rho(x)=a$, hence $x=\bar\rho(x)\in R$ inside $\operatorname{Frac}(S)$. (Use $\rho$ for $\bar\rho$ in case (i).) This proves that $R$ is integrally closed in its fraction field in both cases.

Source: ILO Exposé VI 1.6 (p.70) gives exactly the models k[[P]][[t]] and C[[P]][[t]]/(f) with f≡p mod (P−{0}, t). The item's statement is word for word the model clause of lem-trf-log-regular-completed-chart, nothing is weakened, and normality is correctly marked agent-proved with Kato 1994 WANTED. Step 1: Q=λ(P)×N^n=(λ(G)×Z^n)∩N^{r+n}, and the completion ideal maps onto J. Step 2: both coefficient rings are complete local with finitely generated maximal ideal (0 or pC), so the projection lemma applies. Step 3: Θ has constant coefficient exactly p, while every element of 𝔫² has constant coefficient in p²C and p∉p²C, so the hypersurface criterion applies; r+n=0 gives C/p. Step 4: T∩ΘA=θT follows from the T-linearity of ρ, so R embeds in S with an R-linear retraction. Step 5: regular local ⇒ regular ⇒ normal, and S≅S_m. Step 6: the retraction argument correctly descends integral closure. Both new nodes are true and statement-only, and neither restates the item. Orthant embedding: G is torsion-free, the kernel of the facet map is trivial by sharpness, and it fails without saturation (⟨2,3⟩) or without sharpness. Support projection: the filtrations are cofinal, the image is the closure A_Q, π(ab)=aπ(b) because e∈Q iff f∈Q, and π is not multiplicative for the diagonal M. Duplicate search over orthant, toric, monoid algebra, saturated+normal and supported series found only distinct nodes (fine-monoid-finite-saturation, toric-refinement, completed-chart, complete-toric-monomial-factors). I accept the four declared tool uses, all generic commutative-algebra results from sec-proper-base-change: power-series regularity, the hypersurface criterion, regular local⇒regular, regular⇒normal. No cycle, no SGA, no changes made.
